mt: 'ELECTRONIC BOOK REVIEW' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE JOURNAL AND ITS TWO FOUNDING FIGURES AT THEIR GRAIN; A FOUNDING YEAR THE CENSUS ROW CALLS UNSTATED, FROM WIKIPEDIA; THE MACHINE-WRITING THREAD NOT CARRIED
d: THE JOURNAL, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The Electronic Book Review (ebr) is an open-access, peer-reviewed scholarly journal focused on digital textuality, cyberculture, and the intersection of literature, technology, and the arts.' Key details: 'Established in 1995 by Joseph Tabbi and Mark Amerika', its topics ('critical writing, electronic literature, digital humanities, and peer-to-peer scholarly review alternatives'); format ('dynamic web architectures rather than static issues') and support ('several academic institutions and the Electronic Literature Organization'); an offer on recent essays or submitting. Four cards: the journal's site, Wikipedia, Open Humanities Press, the Electronic Literature Directory.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the journal by its lower-case name, the Overview says what kind of journal it is, who founded it and when, how it is built and who supports it, from its site, its Wikipedia article and two directories.
findings: THE FOUNDING YEAR. 'Established in 1995 by Joseph Tabbi and Mark Amerika'. The Wikipedia card: 'founded in 1995 by Joseph Tabbi and Mark Amerika'; the Open Humanities Press card: 'Publishing open access since 1995 ISSN 1553 1139'. The census row: 'not stated; the oldest thread credits run from 1996 (Writing Postfeminism, fall 1996; Critical Ecologies, winter 1996/97)', its evidence 'Writing Postfeminism was guest edited by Elizabeth Joyce and Gay Lynn Crossley in the fall of 1996.' Both saved pages carry 'ebr@30' in their navigation without a year. The 1995 date stands on two cards whose pages the census did not save.

TWO ROLES MADE ONE. The About page gives the two names separate offices: 'Editor in Chief: Joseph Tabbi ( University of Bergen )' and 'Founding Publisher: Mark Amerika'. The composition makes both founders. Its support line names the ELO alone among 'several academic institutions'; the page lists seven supporters and affiliations, the 'Center for Digital Narrative, University of Bergen' first and 'Consortium for Electronic Literature (CELL)' last, and four sources of partial funding. The first card's snippet keeps the footer's older wording, 'produced and published by the emergent digital literary network'; the About text has 'produced and published by the digital literary network.' The Wikipedia card calls the journal 'monthly'; no saved page gives a frequency.

THE TERMS IN PART. 'open-access, peer-reviewed' is carried; 'diamond', 'ebr does not charge APCs or submission charges.' and 'licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NoDerivatives 4.0 International License.' are not. The ISSN appears on the Open Humanities Press card ('ISSN 1553 1139'), matching the page's 'ISSN: 1553-1139'.

THE MACHINE-WRITING THREAD NOT CARRIED. The census row reads the journal through specific essays: 'AI: A Matter of Significance by Davin Heckman 01-Oct-2026', 'Movie Laughed in Sprocket-Language, or: a Night at the Chatbot by Stuart Moulthrop', 'The Prompt as Practice by Brian Lennon', and Deena Larsen's 'If electronic literature does not exist in Wikipedia, it does not exist for AI or search engines either.' The composition names no thread, no essay and no author beyond the two founding figures; its topics ('digital textuality, cyberculture') do not reach machine composition, and its closing offers 'recent essays published on the journal' without naming one. Its founding year comes, with its second card, from the journal's Wikipedia article.
analysis: The journal composed at its kind and its two founding figures, with a founding year from Wikipedia and Open Humanities Press that the census row records as unstated, and the editor and publisher made co-founders. The machine-writing thread and the essays the census row reads it for are absent.
per_note: Joseph Tabbi and Mark Amerika named; the ELO named; the ISSN on the Open Humanities Press card; the journal's site and Wikipedia carded.
